evidence.claim: Ankor supplies the polity sense. It does not specify empire, monarchy, dynasty, ruler, legal jurisdiction, or territorial size.

evidence.quote: Most Dwarf words have several meanings.
evidence.claim: Roots use the explicitly recorded sense. These compounds are not presented as a recovered complete Khazalid grammar.

evidence.section: Warhammer Armies: Dwarfs (8th Edition, 2014), PDF page 9, opening Dwarf realm description
evidence.claim: Karaz Ankor is an attested descriptive polity name. That canonical realm and its variant spellings are reserved; it is not randomly assigned.

evidence.section: Warhammer Armies: Dwarfs (8th Edition, 2014), PDF page 41, Dwarf Warriors
evidence.quote: show their allegiances through more subtle colours or symbols
evidence.claim: Colour and object motifs are grounded in Dwarf collective identity. Applying such an image to a newly composed realm name is an explicit adaptation, not an assertion that the book prints these combinations.

evidence.section: p.44, Khazalid Glossary: Duraz and Azul
evidence.claim: Stone and metal are attested material senses for symbolic polity images. Azul is not restricted to iron, steel or gromril, and its dependable-person sense is not selected.

evidence.section: p.45, Khazalid Glossary: Galaz and Grungron
evidence.quote: Galaz Gold of particular ornamental value
evidence.claim: Ornamental gold and forge imagery broaden the reviewed craft motifs. These images grant no wealth, mines, craft monopoly or ownership of an actual forge.
A chisel is an attested craft-image alternative to anvil, hammer and gate. A polity using it as a symbolic name is not automatically a miners or masons organisation.

evidence.quote: Wutroth Wood from ancient mountain oak
evidence.claim: The precise material sense is used in the hammer and gate motifs. It does not assert the age of the realm or possession of an ancient forest.
The glossary distinguishes a musical horn from horn material, and attests road and thunder. Selected nouns remain literal word senses inside adapted labels.
The selected moonlight sense and the printed material, shadow, work and sunrise nouns add distinct concepts. No generic machine, dawn-direction, geology or ancestry meaning is invented.

The conjunction explicitly pairs two reviewed images. Thrag means wound, Thrynaz includes laws, Tiwaz includes rest and Skaud includes song. These are not new translations for hospital, government or tavern.

High-resolution printed text confirms Zunthrum with n. Spear, money, sunset, remembering and gift are independently attested; none assigns actual stock, wealth, a historical event or a commemorated person.
